Recovery after airway surgery in bulldogs

The first seventy-two hours after soft palate and nostril surgery decide the outcome. Swelling peaks in that window, so the dog sleeps propped up, eats soft food and wears a harness instead of a collar. Breathing effort should improve every day; if it worsens, that is the call to make immediately.

Regurgitation in the first week is common and usually settles. Persistent regurgitation after two weeks suggests a gastrointestinal component and is the reason we recommend endoscopy in some bulldogs rather than repeating airway surgery.

Exercise restarts gradually at day fourteen, in short lead walks during the cool part of the day. Heat is the single biggest risk for a brachycephalic dog in recovery, and Los Angeles afternoons in summer are more than enough to cause a problem.

Stitches are absorbable. The recheck at day fourteen confirms healing of the palate and the nares.
